variants.title: Take a proposal to the actuator
variants.context: The learned policy proposes and independent software holds authority. A versioned sensor frame feeds the estimator, the policy proposes a short action, the safety gate authorizes it, the trajectory controller executes, and the trace feeds recovery.
variants.prompt: A mobile manipulator is asked to pick a box from a shelf. Put the execution path in order.

items.text: Estimate the task-relevant scene, track uncertainty, and check whether the previous action actually succeeded.
Propose one short action with confidence, preconditions, target frame, and an expiry.
Execute deterministic actuator commands while monitoring tracking error and keeping the ability to cancel.
Record the proposal, verdict, motion, and outcome so divergence can trigger fallback and replay.
Authorize it against freshness, zone, collision, speed, force, and human proximity in the versioned envelope.
Build a versioned sensor frame with synchronized observations, timestamps, calibration identity, and health flags.

variants.hint: Which stage can stop the motion without asking the learned policy?
variants.explanation: No model proposal carries physical authority on its own, so an independent gate and controller sit between the policy and the actuator.

variants.title: Take a proposal to the actuator
variants.context: The learned policy proposes and independent software holds authority. A versioned sensor frame feeds the estimator, the policy proposes a short action, the safety gate authorizes it, the trajectory controller executes, and the trace feeds recovery.
variants.prompt: A depth frame arrives 400 ms late and the policy proposes a grasp based on it. Put the path in order for that proposal.

items.text: Estimate the scene while preserving the ambiguity that the stale depth leaves behind.
Reject the proposal at the gate because the evidence is older than the freshness boundary.
Record the rejection and require the next proposal to reference reacquired observations.
Build the sensor frame and mark the depth stream's timestamp and health flag.
Hold the current safe state through the controller instead of extrapolating the motion.
Propose the grasp with its confidence, target frame, and expiry attached.

variants.hint: Freshness is checked by the layer that owns authority, not by the layer that proposed.
variants.explanation: Stale evidence means the proposal is no longer about the current world, so the safe state is held until observations are reacquired.

variants.title: Take a proposal to the actuator
variants.context: The learned policy proposes and independent software holds authority. A versioned sensor frame feeds the estimator, the policy proposes a short action, the safety gate authorizes it, the trajectory controller executes, and the trace feeds recovery.
variants.prompt: During a placement the measured force spikes and tracking error grows. Put the path in order for that cycle.

items.text: Preserve the force, command, and trajectory traces for review and replay.
Estimate that the contact does not match the expected outcome of the previous action.
Propose no continuation of the old plan, since the world has changed since it was authorized.
Limit or remove actuator authority through the controller or hardware path.
Build the sensor frame carrying force, position, and velocity at the highest available rate.

variants.hint: An old plan does not survive a world that has changed underneath it.
variants.explanation: Divergence between intent and outcome ends the plan, and authority is removed through the controller or hardware rather than by the policy.

variants.title: Stage the evidence
variants.context: Evidence is staged: sweep variations in replay and simulation, exercise the real stack in hardware-in-the-loop, run guarded physical trials at low energy, then expand one regime at a time. Simulation is a discovery layer, not final evidence.
variants.prompt: A new grasping policy passed in simulation. Put the evaluation stages in order before it drives a real robot at production speed.

items.text: Expand one regime at a time, promoting only demonstrated objects, environments, payloads, and speeds.
Sweep object, lighting, instruction, contact, timing, sensor, and network variations in replay and simulation.
Run software and hardware in the loop with production clocks, calibration, action transforms, and controllers.
Run guarded physical trials at low energy with fixtures, exclusion zones, observers, and stop criteria.

variants.hint: Which stage first involves the real controller and the real clocks?
variants.explanation: Simulation discovers cheap failures, and only the executable stack on real hardware can measure the sim-to-real gap.

variants.title: Stage the evidence
variants.context: Evidence is staged: sweep variations in replay and simulation, exercise the real stack in hardware-in-the-loop, run guarded physical trials at low energy, then expand one regime at a time. Simulation is a discovery layer, not final evidence.
variants.prompt: The same checkpoint is moved to a robot with a different gripper and camera calibration. Put the stages in order.

items.text: Run guarded trials at low energy to confirm contact behavior on the new gripper.
Replay protected traces and sweep variations against the new embodiment's configuration.
Exercise the real stack with the new calibration, action normalizer, controller, and firmware in the loop.
Expand one regime at a time rather than inheriting the previous robot's approved envelope.

variants.hint: Is the same checkpoint on new hardware the same executable policy?
variants.explanation: A checkpoint on a different calibration, normalizer, gripper, or controller is a different executable robot policy and needs its own evidence.

variants.title: Stage the evidence
variants.context: Evidence is staged: sweep variations in replay and simulation, exercise the real stack in hardware-in-the-loop, run guarded physical trials at low energy, then expand one regime at a time. Simulation is a discovery layer, not final evidence.
variants.prompt: A rare high-severity failure appeared once in the field. Put the stages in order for requalifying the fix.

items.text: Repeat it in a guarded physical trial with exclusion zones and explicit stop criteria.
Rerun the case with the production stack in hardware-in-the-loop, including the network path.
Expand back to the affected regime only after the recovery path is demonstrated.
Reproduce the incident in replay and fault injection, then sweep its neighboring conditions.

variants.hint: Rare and severe failures do not get promoted on aggregate success rates.
variants.explanation: Regression evidence walks the same staircase as a new release, because the fix has to be shown on the executable system.

variants.title: Budget the control path
variants.context: Inference may spend only the time left after the physical response reserve. Budget the tail rather than the average, because the robot and everything near it keeps moving while sensing, inference, planning, and communication run.
variants.prompt: A supervisory loop has a 250 ms deadline and requires a 60 ms response reserve. Sensing and communication already consume 40 ms. How many milliseconds are left for inference and planning?
variants.hint: The reserve is spent before any thinking starts.
variants.explanation: Compute may use only the deadline minus the physical response reserve minus the fixed sensing and communication cost.

mistakes.feedback: That subtracts the 60 ms reserve but forgets the 40 ms already spent sensing and communicating.
That subtracts sensing and communication but leaves no response reserve for the fallback to settle.

variants.title: Budget the control path
variants.context: Inference may spend only the time left after the physical response reserve. Budget the tail rather than the average, because the robot and everything near it keeps moving while sensing, inference, planning, and communication run.
variants.prompt: A joint controller runs a 1 kHz servo loop. A remote model returns its answer with a p99 of 120 ms. How many servo cycles pass while the robot waits for that answer?
variants.hint: Work out how long one cycle lasts before counting them.
variants.explanation: A 1 kHz loop updates once per millisecond, so a remote dependency on the action path leaves the local controller alone for many cycles.

mistakes.feedback: That treats a servo cycle as 10 ms; at 1 kHz each cycle is 1 ms.
That treats a servo cycle as 0.1 ms, which is ten times faster than 1 kHz.

variants.title: Budget the control path
variants.context: Inference may spend only the time left after the physical response reserve. Budget the tail rather than the average, because the robot and everything near it keeps moving while sensing, inference, planning, and communication run.
variants.prompt: A mobile robot travels at 1.5 meters per second. Sense-to-command p99 latency is 200 ms and the fallback needs another 300 ms to settle. How many meters does the robot cover before motion stops?
variants.hint: Motion continues through both intervals, not just the slow one.
variants.explanation: Motion exposure is speed times the full sense-to-stop time, which is why the deadline budget must include the fallback settling time.

mistakes.feedback: That counts only the 200 ms of latency and ignores the fallback settling time.
That counts only the 300 ms settling time and ignores the sense-to-command latency.

variants.title: Fill in the action contract
variants.context: A model output is not a command. The action contract carries identity, evidence, intent, validity, and outcome so the authority layer can decide whether the proposal is current, permitted, and safe to execute.
variants.prompt: A VLA policy emits a proposal for the gate to judge. Match each part of the contract to what it carries.

pairs.label: Identity
pairs.detail: Sequence ID, task ID, model version, policy configuration, and embodiment configuration.

pairs.label: Evidence
pairs.detail: Observation timestamp, coordinate frame, calibration version, confidence, and sensor health.

pairs.label: Intent
pairs.detail: Target zone, action type, speed, force, waypoint or trajectory, and expected outcome.

pairs.label: Validity
pairs.detail: Preconditions, expiry, operating-envelope version, and the fallback required after rejection.

pairs.label: Outcome
pairs.detail: Authorization verdict, executed command, controller status, completion evidence, and interventions.

variants.hint: Sort by what the gate needs in order to say no.
variants.explanation: The contract exists so an independent layer can decide whether a proposal is current, permitted, and safe without trusting the policy.

variants.title: Fill in the action contract
variants.context: A model output is not a command. The action contract carries identity, evidence, intent, validity, and outcome so the authority layer can decide whether the proposal is current, permitted, and safe to execute.
variants.prompt: The gate rejects four proposals in one shift. Match each rejection to the contract part that made it possible.

pairs.label: A proposal arrives twice with the same sequence and task ID
pairs.detail: Identity, which exposes the replay before it becomes a second motion.

pairs.label: The referenced camera frame is older than the freshness boundary
pairs.detail: Evidence, which carries the observation timestamp and sensor health.

pairs.label: The requested force exceeds the limit for this contact mode
pairs.detail: Intent, which states speed, force, and the target zone up front.

pairs.label: The proposal is presented after its expiry has passed
pairs.detail: Validity, which bounds how long a proposal may be executed.

variants.hint: Each rejection needs one specific field to have been recorded.
variants.explanation: A proposal without identity, evidence, intent, and validity cannot be rejected on principle, so the gate would be forced to trust it.

variants.title: Fill in the action contract
variants.context: A model output is not a command. The action contract carries identity, evidence, intent, validity, and outcome so the authority layer can decide whether the proposal is current, permitted, and safe to execute.
variants.prompt: A team is tempted to drop fields to shorten the message. Match each omission to the failure it would permit.

pairs.label: Dropping the expiry from the proposal
pairs.detail: A stale action executes after the world has already moved.

pairs.label: Dropping the calibration version from the evidence
pairs.detail: A proposal is judged in a frame that no longer matches the robot.

pairs.label: Dropping the sequence ID from the identity
pairs.detail: A replayed message runs a second, unintended motion.

pairs.label: Dropping the executed command from the outcome
pairs.detail: An incident trace cannot show what the actuator was actually told to do.

variants.hint: Ask what an investigator or a gate loses with each field.
variants.explanation: Each contract field either blocks a specific unsafe execution or preserves the evidence needed to explain one afterward.

variants.title: Choose the runtime response
variants.context: The dangerous state is granting motion authority after the evidence or assumptions stop being valid. Each failure class has a designed response, and an uncalibrated confidence score is never permission for more motion.
variants.prompt: The link to the remote model service degrades and responses arrive well past the deadline while the robot is mid-task. What is the designed response?
options: Cancel remote authority at a bounded timeout and continue only a local behavior with known stopping properties.
Queue the late responses and execute them in order once the connection has recovered.
Extrapolate the last accepted proposal until the service catches up with the current task.
optionFeedback: Correct: remote authority expires at a bounded timeout, and degradation continues through a local behavior whose stopping is known.
Executing queued responses applies decisions made about a world that has since moved on.
Extrapolation grants motion authority on evidence that is no longer valid, which is the failure this design prevents.
variants.hint: What happens to authority when the deadline passes?
variants.explanation: Remote reasoning must never own a motion deadline the local robot cannot survive, so authority expires and a local behavior takes over.

variants.title: Choose the runtime response
variants.context: The dangerous state is granting motion authority after the evidence or assumptions stop being valid. Each failure class has a designed response, and an uncalibrated confidence score is never permission for more motion.
variants.prompt: The policy meets an object and lighting combination outside its demonstrated regime, yet it reports a high confidence score. What should the runtime do?
options: Abstain or narrow capability and request approval, since confidence is not permission for more motion.
Allow the motion at reduced speed, since a high confidence score indicates the scene is understood.
Allow the motion and rely on the trace to reveal any problem during the post-run review.
optionFeedback: Correct: an out-of-distribution scene calls for abstention, narrowed capability, or approval, not a self-reported score.
Reduced speed still grants motion authority based on a score that has no calibration outside the training regime.
Reviewing traces afterwards cannot undo a physical effect that has already happened.
variants.hint: Who is checking the checker in this scenario?
variants.explanation: An uncalibrated confidence score is not evidence, so independent monitors and abstention govern out-of-distribution scenes.

variants.title: Choose the runtime response
variants.context: The dangerous state is granting motion authority after the evidence or assumptions stop being valid. Each failure class has a designed response, and an uncalibrated confidence score is never permission for more motion.
variants.prompt: A gripper meets unexpected contact and the tracking error grows while the operator is 20 seconds away from taking control. What is the correct immediate response?
options: Wait for the operator to take control, since a person can judge the contact better than the stack can.
Remove or limit actuator authority locally and preserve the force and trajectory traces at full rate.
Let the policy propose a corrective motion, since it has the freshest view of the contact.
optionFeedback: A handoff cannot be the only response inside a short hazard window, because the hazard resolves long before the operator arrives.
Correct: the controller or hardware path limits authority immediately, and the local safe state is entered before anyone waits.
The policy that proposed the diverging motion is the wrong authority to grant it a correction.
variants.hint: Compare the length of the hazard window with the operator response time.
variants.explanation: Local safe state comes first and the handoff second, since a response that shares the policy's failure mode or arrives late is no response.
